title: Green wins from pole as late punctures strike Mercedes at Zandvoort
dek: Jamie Green led from pole to win Zandvoort Race 2 for Audi by 9.731 seconds, as late punctures cost Mercedes-AMG's Wickens and Vietoris the podium and Marco Wittmann kept the championship lead.

chapters.title: A tighter title fight after Saturday
text: Sunday's race followed a Saturday that had tightened the championship. Robert Wickens won Race 1 from pole for Mercedes-AMG, and Marco Wittmann's second place stretched his lead to 93 points against Wickens's 83, while Audi lost ground when Edoardo Mortara and Nico Müller were given drive-through penalties. Mortara and Jamie Green went into Sunday level on 73 points. The second race ran for 60 minutes and carried a mandatory pit stop, which offered a chance to gain places on a circuit where passing is so hard. René Rast stepped in to drive the Rosberg Audi #72, after Adrien Tambay did not start.

chapters.title: Green breaks Mercedes's grip on the weekend
text: Mercedes-AMG had been fastest in every session of the weekend, but Green ended that run with a single push lap of 1m30.696s, 0.079 seconds quicker than Gary Paffett's Mercedes-AMG. Christian Vietoris was third, 0.096 seconds off pole, and Mortara answered Saturday's penalty with fourth place, 0.163 seconds back and the second-best Audi. Wickens was fifth at 0.241 seconds, Timo Glock the leading BMW in sixth, and Wittmann seventh at 0.350 seconds. Esteban Ocon, Mattias Ekström and Müller completed the top ten.

Green's lap was briefly under investigation after he was caught speeding in the pit lane, at 65 km/h in a 60 km/h limit. The stewards fined him 250 euros and left the grid unchanged, which made him the first driver to take a second pole position of the season, after nine earlier qualifying sessions had produced nine different fastest drivers.

Daniel Juncadella ran into the gravel in the opening minutes, which caused a short red flag, and set no time; his Mercedes-AMG #12 was due to start last. Rast, replacing Tambay, qualified 22nd at 1m32.079s, ahead of only Maximilian Götz and Juncadella.

chapters.title: Green defends against a Mercedes trio
text: Green kept the lead at the start, but the first stint was a hard defence. Wickens, Paffett and Vietoris queued up behind the Audi, and Wickens looked to the inside at Tarzanbocht and briefly drew alongside, but Green defended and kept the place. The drivers could not use DRS in the early part of the race, because the timing system was not transmitting the gaps between cars. Green said afterwards that Wickens and Paffett had filled his mirrors and that he had expected a tough afternoon.
Timo Scheider's Phoenix Audi #10 was the first car out, stopping after three laps.

chapters.title: Green and Wickens stop together, and Green gets the better of it
text: Green and Wickens made their mandatory stops together at the end of the first stint, and Green rejoined roughly a second ahead. He then built his advantage as the leaders came up to cars that had yet to make their own stops, and the key moment was a clean pass on Juncadella's Mercedes-AMG at Tarzan. Green said his second set of tyres worked better than the first and that he controlled the gap from there.

Once the traffic had cleared, Green was almost three seconds clear, with Wickens leading Paffett, Vietoris and Mortara. Ekström, who made a late stop from a lead gained while others pitted, used fresh tyres to climb back through the order.

chapters.title: Two Mercedes-AMG cars fall from the podium places
text: With a few laps to run, the race turned. Wickens, running second, suffered a front-left puncture and was sent onto the grass at one of the fast right-handers. He had to make an unplanned stop and rejoined to finish 16th, 40.345 seconds behind Green. Shortly afterwards Vietoris, who had been in the top four, slowed with a puncture of his own and was out after 35 laps.
Paffett was left to take second, Mortara moved up onto the podium, and Wittmann inherited fourth.

chapters.title: Green wins by 9.731 seconds
text: Green took the flag after 39 laps in 1h01m54.997s, his first win of 2016 and the 13th of his DTM career, 9.731 seconds clear of Paffett. Mortara was third, 14.153 seconds behind the winner, and Wittmann fourth at 18.833 seconds, the leading BMW. Müller, Glock and Ekström followed, with Paul di Resta eighth, Lucas Auer ninth and Tom Blomqvist tenth. Martin Tomczyk finished 11th, just outside the points.

Juncadella set the fastest lap of the race, a 1m33.087s on lap 20, and fought from the back of the grid to 12th. Rast completed the race in 19th. Besides Vietoris and Scheider, Maxime Martin, Miguel Molina and Götz also failed to finish.

chapters.title: Green moves to second as Mercedes counts the cost
text: Green's win lifted him to second in the championship on 98 points, seven behind Wittmann. He said he had feared a hard race with Wickens and Paffett so close early on, but that the second set of tyres after the stop was better and the pace stronger, which allowed him to control the gap and even extend it. Audi's DTM boss Dieter Gass called the result a balm after the disappointment of Saturday, and Green, delighted to win at Zandvoort after waiting many years for it, celebrated with doughnuts on the track for the Audi mechanics.

For Mercedes-AMG the afternoon was costly. Mercedes DTM chief Ulrich Fritz called it very bitter, saying the cars had been very good and that to lose so many points in that way was a pity. Wickens dropped from second to fourth in the standings, with 83 points and 22 behind Wittmann. Paffett, who had no problems, called it by far his best weekend of the year and said the title fight remained open.

Wittmann, who had finished second and fourth over the weekend, kept the lead on 105 points. He acknowledged some luck in the rivals' tyre trouble, but said the team had made the most of its possibilities over the weekend and that the championship stayed extremely tight. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt agreed that the fourth, sixth and tenth places of the day, with Glock and Tom Blomqvist scoring alongside Wittmann, were the maximum available. Mortara was third on 88 points, and said Sunday's luck evened out Saturday's misfortune.

The Saturday penalty remained the weekend's sore point for Audi. Mortara maintained that his on-board footage and data log showed he had done nothing wrong. The penalty had been given in error after a technical glitch, and Gass said Mortara had lost at least eight points as a result, but Mortara's points were not restored. About 38,000 spectators attended over the weekend, and the DTM will return after the summer break at Moscow Raceway, with races on 20 and 21 August.

facts.v: Green set pole with a 1m30.696s lap, 0.079 seconds ahead of Paffett, and kept it after a 250-euro fine for speeding in the pit lane.
